newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures slowly firm, most end higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures slowly firm, most end higher.

text.p: A slow grind higher during the afternoon left most U.S. debt futures at higher levels Monday and hugging session highs.

Technical buying coupled with a strong dollar continued to bolster the long end, where order flows picked up slightly near the close as one dealer bought some 2,000 September contracts and helped tug the contract to the day's high.

Some brokers said signs of progress on a federal budget agreement added lift. President Clinton said White House and Congressional Republicans were in the final stages of talks and were on the verge of achieving a balanced budget pact.
One floor broker estimated that volume in September Treasury bond futures Monday totalled some 180,000 contracts.
He attributed the ratchet upward to small covering as shorts, perhaps left from Friday's erosion, capitulated.
In the short end, brokers reported decent order flow but hesitation to take prices too far in either direction before this week's full slate of U.S. economic reports.
They said one dealer, for example, by early afternoon had bought some 6,000 June and 10,000 March Eurodollars but then sold back half that total, all while futures prices barely budged.
"It's just a continuation of last week," said a Eurodollar broker. "Everyone's looking for bargains but no one's willing to press the market too aggressively."
Tuesday's second-quarter U.S. employment cost index is expected to rise 0.8 percent versus a prior rise of 0.6 percent. July U.S. consumer confidence, seen firming to 130.4, also is due Tuesday.

The market also will see how much supply it faces, as Treasury announces its quarterly refunding on Wednesday. Forecasters look for a total package of $40.0 billion, including $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds.

Technically, some chartists said the uptrend in September T-bonds might have stalled and that the contract needs to clear last Wednesday's high at 115-23/32 in order to head higher, perhaps toward 117-00.

September T-bonds rose 13/32 to 115-14/32, 10-year notes rose 6/32 to 110-06/32, munis gained 11/32 to 121-01/32, December T-bills added 0.010 to 94.825, and December Eurodollars gained 0.015 to 94.140. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
